text:
sam: FYI noticed ~15 nodes in us-central1 (rack-r5) drop to PXE fallback after the microcode push at 03:12 UTC. Thermal sensors spike to 85-90C, then kexec/kernel panic, then PXE. Provisioner backlog climbing and retries are doubling cost.

deploy-bot: rollout microcode v1.2.4 started 2026-03-19T03:12:04Z -> target: rack-r5 us-central1-gpu.

nora: ack. which fleet subset? can you paste the node IDs?

sam: node ids: gpu-usc-r5-n[12,13,14,16,18,21,22,23,29,31,33,34,36,38,41]

jorge: quick look at serial logs shows SecureBoot state flipping to "disabled" just before panic on a few nodes. pattern: BMC re-applies microcode -> last-line in serial: "UEFI: SecureBoot: state change request" -> kernel oops -> kexec fallback -> pxeboot.

kai: if secureboot is being toggled that could cause kernel module sig checks to fail and OOPS. do we have the exact firmware blob hash?

sam: firmware hash from deploy-log: sha256: 3f7a9c...a12e (v1.2.4). I can dump more serial logs but it's noisy. here's a condensed snippet:

```
[03:12:57] BMC: flash apply ok
[03:13:02] UEFI: Microcode applied (v=0x24)
[03:13:03] UEFI: SecureBoot: requested action=toggle->disabled
[03:13:05] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference
[03:13:06] kexec: falling back to PXE
```

nora: have we seen secureboot toggles in previous rollouts? not common for microcode. could be an interaction with our bootloader config.

jorge: Agree. Also seeing athermal drift entries from the BMC sensor plugin right before the toggle; could be a sensor glitch that triggers a recovery path which includes toggling secureboot flags.

kai: Actionable steps I suggest now:
- stop further rollout to us-central1 (abort remaining hosts in deploy)
- run canary rollback of microcode on r5
- force BMC watchdog resets on affected hosts (ipmitool/chassis rstr)
- patch provisioning policy to disable automatic PXE fallback for the GPU pool until stable (reduce cost from retries)

sam: trying abort now -> `deployctl abort --rollout 3f7a9c --region us-central1`

deploy-bot: rollout 3f7a9c aborted for region us-central1 at 03:21:11Z. remaining hosts skipped.

infra-oncall: I'm on it. starting canary rollback to v1.2.3 on gpu-usc-r5-n12,n13,n14. also applying temporary provisioning flag: `allow_pxe_fallback=false` for pool gpu-usc-r5. Will monitor.

sam: note on cost: provisioner retries are requeuing ~200 tasks in the last 30m; estimating ~2.1x normal GPU provisioning egress and reprovisioning costs. I'll open a billing alert ticket.

nora: thanks. can infra-oncall include runbook steps for manual BMC reset? if BMC sensor is flaky we should validate therm readouts before toggling secureboot.

infra-oncall: runbook snippet I'm executing now:
```
# quick BMC reset (serial console):
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS chassis power cycle
# force firmware rollback:
flashctl rollback --slot primary --to sha:9b2e1c
# provisioning policy cmd:
provctl set-pool-config gpu-usc-r5 allow_pxe_fallback=false --dry-run && provctl set-pool-config gpu-usc-r5 allow_pxe_fallback=false --apply
```

jorge: if rollback fixes nodes, we should collect a full sensor dump and run the secureboot flag transition trace to file. I'll prepare a small script to correlate sensor timestamps with the secureboot change events.

kai: also flag to security: if secureboot is toggling unexpectedly we need to ensure we're not leaving nodes in a less secure state. please cc: secops.

sam: opened tracking ticket INF-7621 and billing alert BL-894. tagging @secops in ticket.

infra-oncall: update 03:38Z: canary rollback applied to n12,n13,n14; two of three came up healthy, sensors stable ~58C, secureboot remained enabled during boot. provisioning backlog dropped ~40% after disabling PXE fallback.

nora: great. can we schedule a full rollback for the rest of r5 after validation window (30m)?

infra-oncall: scheduling full rollback to v1.2.3 for remaining affected nodes at 04:05Z with oncall present. I'll keep prov fallback disabled until post-mortem.

sam: thanks. keep updates here. once stable we'll run regression tests on secureboot state transitions. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: final update 03:55Z: full rollback queued, healthchecks passing on first wave, provisioning costs trending back to normal. closing active incident; postmortem to follow in incidents channel.
